title: Describe paving machine equipment and attachments
intro: A paver consists of a tractor that receives and moves material and a screed that forms the mat. Equipment choice depends on the work, access, production and required result—not only the nominal paving width.

sections.title: Describe types of paving machines
sections.text: Pavers range from compact pathway or shoulder machines to highway-class equipment. Common nominal categories include 8 ft and 10 ft machines, but actual minimum/maximum widths, extensions and transport dimensions depend on the model. Compare work width, production, turning space, support, transport and fitted options. Light, medium and highway duty describe broad applications rather than interchangeable operating limits. Match the OMM to model, serial range and configuration.

sections.title: Describe major components
sections.text: Identify the tractor’s hopper and wings, push rollers/truck interface, slat conveyors or other fitted feed system, augers, engine, hydraulics, undercarriage, operator station and grade/slope controls. Wheeled, rubber-tracked and steel-tracked arrangements differ. Identify the screed’s tow arms/tow points, main plate, extensions, end gates, heating and vibration/tamper equipment where fitted. Conveyors move material toward the screed; augers spread it; the screed forms the layer. Do not confuse a feed sensor with a grade sensor.

sections.title: Describe attachments
sections.text: A pickup machine can collect a windrow placed by an appropriate delivery system and feed the paver. A material-transfer vehicle or hopper insert may buffer supply or remix material, depending on design. These can reduce certain handling problems but do not guarantee freedom from segregation or a universal productivity increase. Belly-dump and end-dump arrangements require different work plans. Check compatibility, added weight, clearance and operating instructions for every attachment.

worked.title: Two sensor jobs
worked.case: A diagram labels one sensor near the auger and another following a reference beside the machine.
worked.solution: The feed sensor can control the material supply in its assigned zone; a grade sensor follows a reference for elevation control. Confirm the actual model and function from the manual. Similar-looking sensors do not necessarily control the same system.

activities.prompt: Label ten parts on the supplied paver figure and state each function.
activities.answer: Use hopper, wings, push rollers, conveyors, augers, tracks/wheels, operator station, tow arms, screed plate and end gates or other correctly identified visible parts. Explain functions using the diagram and model scope.
activities.title: Label ten parts on the supplied paver figure and state each function.

activities.prompt: Convert nominal 8 ft and 10 ft widths to metres. Do these establish the actual screed settings?
activities.answer: 8 × 0.3048 = 2.4384 m; 10 × 0.3048 = 3.048 m. These conversions do not establish a particular machine’s working width or setting.

activities.prompt: Ask an AI to create a component table from the supplied figure and caption. How will you audit it?
activities.answer: Require visible labels, functions and source/page references; verify every row against the image/manual. Mark hidden or unclear parts as unconfirmed. Do not accept invented labels or model-specific settings. Save the checked table with its source credit.
